NORTH WILDWOOD — Wildwood is going red again.
This time for a Republican rally roaring back to the same Jersey Shore hotspot where Donald Trump once drew a sea of MAGA faithful.
on Friday, the Cape May Regular Republican Organization hosts their "America First — Return to the Wildwoods Rally" at the Seaport Pier in North Wildwood from 4 to 7 p.m.
Unlike the previous events, there is no advance ticketing, with a much smaller crowd.
Trump hosted a rally at the Wildwood Convention Center in January 2020 just before the pandemic set in, that drew an estimated 15,000 people.
As a candidate, Trump appeared at a rally on the beach in May 2024.
Depending on the count, anywhere from 20,000 to 100,000 came to the event or were in Wildwood that day.
North Wildwood Mayor Patrick Rosenello is looking forward to being the first speaker and welcoming Republicans to his city.

Jeff Van Drew, R-N.J. 2nd District, conservative media personality Benny Johnson, Cape May County GOP Chairman Mike Donohue, conservative organizer Scott Pressler and Assemblyman Paul Kanitra, R-Ocean.

With expectations that over 50% of eligible voters will decide not to cast a ballot in this year's election, the freshman legislator hopes to deliver a message of the importance of casting a ballot.
"My intent is to rile everybody up, get everybody else to rile their friends and family up and make sure that we turn out the vote," Kanitra said.
But what about those Republicans not pleased with their choice of candidate?
"This is a very clear equation.

If you are a conservative, if you are a Republican, if you like President Trump, if you dislike Governor Murphy and his policies, you not turning out to vote is a de facto vote for a liberal, progressive Democrat that will take this state in an incredibly horrible path.
So the only answer is to turn out and vote against that," Kanitra said.
Kanitra said there are rumors of a "special guest" making an appearance but says he does not know who it could be.
The White House had not released the Friday schedule for Trump or Vice President J.D.
Vance as of Thursday afternoon.
Trump is expected to travel to the Middle East for the final steps in the peace agreement between Hamas and Israel.
Rosenello said that semi-retired Fox reporter Steve Doocy will be reporting from the event on Friday.

Thomas Edison demonstrated an incandescent light buib for the first time in October 1879 that was "practical" and could light a home for many hours at his first lab in Menlo Park which is now part of Edison Township, according to the Thomas Edison National Historical Park.
It was there that he and his team that he called "muckers" would create wires, fuses and switches needed to light an entire home.
Edison would later build a bigger lab in West Orange where he worked on the photograph, the motion picture and storage battery.
Edison earned 1,093 United States patents, a record number for one person that still stands.
The George Washington Bridge opened to traffic on Oct. 25, 1931 and was the longest suspension bridge in the world until the Golden Gate Bridge in 1937.
Four lanes carry traffic over the Hudson River between Fort Lee and Manhattan on the upper level with three lanes in each direction on the lower level.
The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey in March finished the replacement of the original 592 steel suspender ropes.
The seven year project is part of the $2 billion "Restoring the George" program.
A live broadcast of the H.G.

Welles science fiction novel "War of the Worlds" during the CBS Radio Network's "Mercury Theatre on the Air" on Oct. 30, 1938 caused panic as listeners thought Martians landed in the Grover's Mills section of West Windsor The show sounded like today's breaking news coverage of a meteorite that landed in a field complete with eyewitness accounts of aliens emerging from spaceships.
The Cherry Hill Mall opened on Oct. 11, 1961 as the first enclosed mall in New Jersey, according to coverage by the Courier-Post.
Designed by James Rouse the mall would have a "tropical plant motif" in two different wings.
The Delaware Mall included a movie theater and community room while thee Penn Mall resemembed a European market.
The mall's original anchors included Strawbridge & Clothier, Woolworth's, S.S.
Kresge, Bamberger's and a Food Fair supermarket.
The 80,000 seat Giants Stadium opened on Oct. 10, 1976 in the Meadowlands of East Rutherford with a 24-14 loss by the Giants.
The Rutgers Scarlet Knights played their first game there on Oct. 23 shutting out Columbia 47-0.
The stadium has been home to the Jets, the USFL's NJ Generals, the WLAF's NY/NJ Knights, the XFL's NY/NJ Hitmen and the UFL's Sentinels.
The Cosmos and Red Bulls soccer teams also called the stadium home.
The stadium also hosted hundreds of concerts from Bruce Springsteen to U2 to Pink Floyd.
It's first concert was the Beach Boys, The Steve Miller Band, Stanky Brown and Pablo Cruise in 1978.
It was also the subject of the urban myth that Teamsters president Jimmy Hoffa was buried under one the end zones.
But a body was not found during the demolition of the stadium.
Giants Stadium's last event was a Jets/Bengals game in Jan. 2010.

After starting out as the Kansas City Scouts and the original Colorado Rockies, the NHL's New Jersey Devils were bought by trucking company owner and Jersey City native John McMullen who moved them to the Brendan Byrne Arena.
The Devils first game in the Meadowlands ended in a 3-3 tie with the Pittsburgh Penguins on Oct. 5, 1982 followed by the team's first win with a 3-2 victory over the Rangers on Oct. 8.
The Purdential Center in Newark became the Devils new home at the start of the 2007-08 season.
Their first game at "The Rock" ended with a 4-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators.

One of the worst disasters in New Jersey history, Superstorm Sandy, or its more formal name Post-Tropical Cyclone Sandy, triggered incredible wind, rain, and storm surge, according to NJ 101.5 Chief Meteorologist Dan Zarrow.
The property damage, infrastructure destruction, and loss of life were nothing short of catastrophic.
The storm's track was a worst-case scenario for the Jersey Shore and made landfall near Brigantine around 7:30 p.m. on Oct. 29. 2012 with 9-foot storm surges.
The highest wind gust recorded was 91 mph in Seaside Heights.
The heaviest rain fell in South Jersey where Stone Harbor picked up a foot of rain.
Over two million households lost power.
Many thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed.
Pieces of barrier islands were completely isolated from the mainland.
The vast majority of schools and businesses were closed statewide.
Broken gas mains led to fires.
Along its entire path, Sandy's estimated sustained winds peaked at 115 mph.
Its lowest barometric pressure dipped to 940 millibars.
One EF-0 tornado was confirmed near Somerset, Bermuda.The storm's death toll was 234 with damage totalling $68.7 billion, the second costliest storm in US history.
Same sex marriages becamee legally recognized in New Jersey on Oct. 21, 2013 after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that gay and lesbian Americans have the same right to marry as any other couples.
Civil unions became legal in 2006 with the passage of the Civil Union Act.
